chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asam, from Misma ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sent Surah al-Bara'ah (Disavowal) with Ali (peace be upon him), he sent some people with him, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'One who lets himself be made a captive without having sustained any heavy injuries, so he is not from us (peace be upon him and his family).'

key_terms.اسْتَأْسَرَ: To let oneself be made a captive or prisoner
key_terms.بَرَاءَةَ: Surah al-Bara'ah (Disavowal), referring to Chapter 9 of the Quran

ai.seo_question: What is the criterion for determining if a soldier is 'from us' based on their conduct in battle?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in *Al-Kafi*, highlights the Prophet’s directive to Ali (AS) during the conquest of Mecca, establishing a specific criterion for distinguishing true martial valor from cowardice. In Shia scholarly tradition, the phrase 'not from us' (*faysa minna*) is interpreted not merely as a general exclusion but as a specific indicator of a lack of *firasah* (spiritual insight) and endurance, where surrender without significant injury (*jirahat muthqilah*) signifies a failure to uphold the expected standard of steadfastness in the path of God.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman Al Asamma, from Misma’a Bin Abdul Malik, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> sent with the disavowment (Chapter 9:1) along with Ali<sup>asws</sup>, sent some people with him<sup>asws</sup>, and Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Then one who lets himself be made a captive without having sustained any heavy injuries, so he is not from us<sup>saww</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Shammun from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm from Misma’ ibn ‘Abd al-Malik who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that when the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, sent through Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, the declaration of the abrogation of peace treaty to be announce in Makkah, he sent along with him a group of people.
The Messenger of Allah then said (to them), ‘Those who turn themselves into captivity without having sustained a disabling wound are not of our people.’”
